pinterest.title: Marriage Licence and Marriage Certificate Compared
pinterest.description: A licence permits a marriage and a certificate records one. Australia has no licence, so every document you hold is a certificate, and they are not equal. As at November 2026, the certificate signed on the day is ceremonial. The official certificate comes from the state or territory registry, and it is the one you need to change your name or prove you are married. Your celebrant can apply for it on your behalf. Our guide explains the difference.

pinterest.title: How Marriage Licences Work in New Zealand and Hawaii
pinterest.description: Marrying abroad? The destination's law decides the paperwork. As at November 2026, in New Zealand you arrange a marriage licence at least 3 working days before the wedding, and it expires after 3 months. In Hawaii you apply online, then appear together in person before an agent no sooner than 30 days before the ceremony, which must take place within 30 days of picking up the licence. Our guide covers recognition back in Australia too. General information, not legal advice.

slides: Searching for a marriage licence in Australia? There is none to apply for.
As at November 2026, the step before an Australian wedding is a Notice of Intended Marriage, given to your authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the day.
You then marry before that celebrant and 2 witnesses aged over 18. Within 14 days, the celebrant submits the paperwork to the registry in your state or territory.
A licence permits a marriage. A certificate records one. The certificate signed on the day is ceremonial. The official one comes from the registry, and it is the one you need to change your name.
Marrying abroad? The destination's law takes over. New Zealand and Hawaii issue marriage licences through their own authorities, each with its own timing rules.
An overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia. It is generally recognised here if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.
So the first decision is which country makes your marriage legal. Marry at home and celebrate abroad, or marry under your destination's law.
Once you have chosen, tell us about the celebration. A Wedded Advisor will talk through the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you. Send us a message or tap the link in bio.
instagram_carousel.caption:
Searching for a marriage licence in Australia? There is none to apply for.

As at November 2026, you give a Notice of Intended Marriage to an authorised marriage celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding. You marry before that celebrant and 2 witnesses, and within 14 days the celebrant submits the paperwork to the registry of births, deaths and marriages in your state or territory.

A licence permits a marriage, a certificate records one. The certificate you sign on the day is ceremonial. The official certificate comes from the registry, and it is the one you need to change your name or prove you are married.

Marrying abroad? The destination's law takes over. New Zealand and Hawaii issue marriage licences through their own authorities, each with its own timing rules. An overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia, so plan the name change separately and ask your local registry before you travel.

The first decision is which country makes your marriage legal: Australia, with a symbolic ceremony abroad, or your destination, under its own law. Our new guide sets out both paths. This is general information as at November 2026, not legal advice.

The notice, the celebrant and the registry stay with you. For the celebration abroad, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, as your single point of contact. Send us a message, and find the full guide at the link in our bio.
